question: A nucleus has radius proportional to $A^{1/3}$, but its binding energy depends on nuclear mass defect. Explain why nuclear size alone cannot decide nuclear stability.

options.A: Nuclear stability is decided only by radius; a larger nucleus is always more stable.
options.B: Nuclear size directly gives the mass defect, so binding energy per nucleon is unnecessary.
options.C: The relation $R=R_0A^{1/3}$ describes nuclear size, whereas stability depends mainly on binding energy per nucleon, which is determined by mass defect. A nucleus is more stable when its nucleons are more strongly bound on average.
options.D: Nuclear stability depends only on the total number of nucleons, not on binding energy.
